\section{Introduction}

The truncated Wigner approximation (TWA) propagates classical trajectories~\cite{P2010}.
The memory kernel $K$ of \cref{eq:a} describes how the bath responds after a lag $\tau$, e.g. in the Hubbard model.
\Cref{eq:a} gives the kernel, and the ratio is 1:4 in the notation of Ref.~\cite{X}.
\begin{equation}
  K(\tau)=\theta(\tau)\sin\omega\tau \label{eq:a}
\end{equation}
Here $\theta$ is the step function and $\omega$ the bath frequency.
Using TWA, we compute the damping at $T=0.5$ for two baths.
